summary.name: How to set and monitor SLAs (SysAdvent Day 20)
summary.one_liner: A 2016 SysAdvent article by Datadog's Emily Chang explaining how to collect metrics to define SLAs, SLOs and SLIs, then build dashboards and alerts to monitor them.
use_cases: Defining realistic SLAs from historical latency data
Setting internal SLOs stricter than external SLAs
Correlating performance spikes with code releases
summary.what_it_does: The article defines SLA, SLO and SLI following the Google SRE book and recommends collecting user-facing metrics (uptime, response time) and internal metrics before setting objectives. It advises looking at latency distributions with percentiles rather than averages, using a worked example of a 99th-percentile API latency target. It describes creating dashboards that overlay code releases as events and combine end-user metrics with subcomponent metrics such as HAProxy and Gunicorn. It also covers alert classification into record, notification and page levels, with examples of SLO-based and resource-based alerts.
notable: Uses percentile-based latency analysis (p50, p95, p99) instead of averages
Recommends internal SLOs stricter than external SLAs to leave time to react
Overlays code release events on metric graphs for correlation
Tiered alerting: record, notification, or page based on urgency
caveats: Article is a guide, not a tool; examples use Datadog products and screenshots
Written in 2016; specific tools and figures reflect that period
